entry.title: Three Bitcoin Core security advisories
entry.summary:
Three security vulnerabilities have been identified and detailed for Bitcoin Core, each posing distinct risks to the network. These issues have been addressed in Bitcoin Core version 29.2 and all subsequent 29.x releases, as well as in version 30.0 and later.
The first vulnerability, CVE-2025-62861, involves a mempool inconsistency bug related to reorganization handling. This flaw can be exploited by attackers to prevent miners from obtaining valid block templates, potentially disrupting block production. Comprehensive information about this issue is provided on the [official disclosure page](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/10/disclose-cve-2025-62861/).
The second vulnerability, CVE-2025-62860, pertains to the incorrect application of whitelist privileges on inbound Tor connections. This misconfiguration opens up the possibility for denial-of-service attacks against affected nodes or may lead to unintended leaks of internal state data. Further technical details and guidance regarding this vulnerability are available at the [corresponding advisory](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/10/disclose-cve-2025-62860/).
CVE-2025-62859, the third vulnerability, arises from a misplaced witness malleation check. Exploiting this weakness enables malicious peers to stall block processing, undermining the normal operation of the node. The full disclosure can be reviewed [here](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/10/disclose-cve-2025-62859/).
To ensure robust network security and uninterrupted service, users and node operators are strongly encouraged to upgrade to the latest supported releases that contain these critical patches. Additional insights into Bitcoin Core's security disclosure practices, along with historical advisories, can be found on the [security advisories page](https://bitcoincore.org/en/security-advisories/).
